asean-workbook-reg-0616-thailand-tis-dlt.summary: Overview entry for Thailand's national (TIS/DLT) vehicle and component conformity framework, covering market access and type approval for vehicles and components manufactured, imported or sold in Thailand. The text is a general description that points to specific TIS/DLT instruments and does not itself set detailed requirements.
asean-workbook-reg-0616-thailand-tis-dlt._why: Body is a generic template: regulated area, applicability and compliance-intent headings only.

br-contran-949.summary: Brazilian CONTRAN Resolution 949/2022 (28 March 2022) sets occupant protection requirements for side impact against a deformable barrier and against a pole, for domestic and imported automobiles, light trucks, vans and utility vehicles. Results of tests under UN technical regulations or North American standards are accepted as an alternative. Entry into force 1 April 2022, with phased application dates for the barrier requirements (2020, 2024) and pole requirements (2026, 2030).

br-contran-970.summary: Brazilian CONTRAN Resolution 970/2022 (20 June 2022) sets the technical characteristics and specifications of vehicle lighting and signalling systems and devices, and governs the use of special lamps on vehicles. It applies to automobiles, light trucks, trucks, truck tractors, buses, minibuses, trailers and semi-trailers, and accepts UN/UNECE or FMVSS test results as an alternative. Entry into force 1 July 2022.

br-ibama-in-3.summary: IBAMA Normative Instruction 3/2021 sets the requirements and criteria for evaluating light passenger and light commercial vehicles by real driving emissions (RDE) testing for PROCONVE phases L7 and L8, under Chapter VIII of CONAMA Resolution 492/2018. The technical requirements are in its annex, which also covers emissions family grouping. It enters into force 10 days after publication.
br-ibama-in-3._why: Arts. 1 and 2 and the annex of the text.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s104.summary: Section 104 of Canada's Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations (CMVSS 104) requires every vehicle to have a power-driven windshield wiping system with at least two speeds, one of at least 45 cycles per minute, a speed of at least 20 cycles per minute, and at least 15 cycles per minute between the highest and a lower speed. Passenger cars and three-wheeled vehicles must wipe minimum percentages of areas A, B and C per SAE J903a. Every vehicle must also have a washer system meeting SAE J942.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s131.summary: Section 131 of Canada's Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations applies to school buses other than multifunction school activity buses. It requires one or two stop signal arms conforming to TSD 131. If the bus has an image recording system for vehicles passing while the red warning lamps are on, the system must record rear licence plates automatically and operate from -40 to 40 degrees C. A bilingual warning label is required; a transitional provision runs until 1 November 2027.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s201.summary: Section 201 of Canada's Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations applies to passenger cars and to multi-purpose passenger vehicles, trucks and buses with a GVWR of 4 536 kg or less. It requires the instrument panel within the head impact area to decelerate a 6.8 kg head form no more than 80 g continuously for over 3 ms, when struck at 19.3 km/h (with an air bag and Type 2 belt at the right front seat) or 24 km/h otherwise. The test follows SAE J921b.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s206.summary: Section 206 of Canada's Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations requires buses of 4 536 kg GVWR or less, enclosed motorcycles, multi-purpose passenger vehicles, three-wheeled vehicles, passenger cars and trucks that have side or back doors to meet either TSD 206 (Door Locks and Door Retention Components) or United Nations Regulation No. 11 as amended by the 03 or 04 series of amendments.
ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s206._why: s. 206(1); the text itself adopts UN R11.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s208.summary: Section 208 of Canada's Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations specifies which seat belt assemblies (Type 1 or Type 2, manual, with emergency- or automatic-locking retractors, and whether detachable) must be installed at each designated seating position. Requirements vary by vehicle type: enclosed motorcycles, passenger cars and three-wheeled vehicles, trucks and multi-purpose passenger vehicles with GVWR of 4 536 kg or less, and those above 4 536 kg.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s210.summary: Section 210 of Canada's Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations requires seat belt anchorages at each designated seating position fitted with a belt under section 208: pelvic anchorages for a Type 1 assembly, combined pelvic and upper torso anchorages for Type 2. The anchorages and owner's manual must conform to TSD 210 for three-wheeled vehicles, passenger cars, multipurpose passenger vehicles, non-school buses and trucks up to 4 536 kg GVWR; enclosed motorcycles need only the S4.2 strength test. A transitional provision runs to 1 September 2020.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s210-2.summary: Section 210.2 of Canada's Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations applies to passenger cars, three-wheeled vehicles, multi-purpose passenger vehicles and trucks up to 3 856 kg GVWR and 2 495 kg unloaded weight, buses up to 4 536 kg GVWR, and school buses, with exclusions such as walk-in vans and hearses. It sets requirements for lower universal anchorage systems (two 6 mm horizontal bars) to attach child restraints.
ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s210-2._why: s. 210.2(1)-(3); body concerns child-restraint anchorages, not air bags.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s212.summary: Section 212 of Canada's Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations requires passenger cars, and trucks, buses and multi-purpose passenger vehicles of 4 536 kg GVWR or less, to conform to TSD 212 (Windshield Mounting). Forward control configuration vehicles, open-body vehicles with a fold-down or removable windshield and, for non-cars, walk-in vans are excluded.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s213-4.summary: Section 213.4 of Canada's Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations sets requirements for built-in restraint systems and built-in booster seats, tested under Test Method 213.4 (November 2012). Materials must meet TSD 302 flammability requirements, and belts, buckles and webbing must meet specified TSD 209 provisions. Buckle release forces and webbing breaking strength (at least 11 000 N) are specified.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s215.summary: Section 215 of Canada's Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations requires passenger cars to be fitted with bumpers conforming either to UN Regulation No. 42 (paragraph 6 and the Annex 3 low-speed impact test, 00 series, version of 12 June 2007) or to 49 CFR Part 581 (United States). Conformity has been required since 1 September 2009.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s216.summary: Section 216 of Canada's Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations requires passenger cars, multi-purpose passenger vehicles, trucks and buses of 4 536 kg GVWR or less to conform to TSD 216 (Roof Crush Resistance). School buses, convertibles and trucks over 2 722 kg built from a cutaway chassis are excluded; some multi-stage or altered-roof vehicles may alternatively meet TSD 220.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s219.summary: Section 219 of Canada's Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations requires passenger cars, and trucks, buses and multi-purpose passenger vehicles of 4 536 kg GVWR or less, to conform to TSD 219 (Windshield Zone Intrusion). Forward control configuration vehicles, open-body vehicles with a fold-down or removable windshield and, for non-cars, walk-in vans are excluded.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s301.summary: Section 301 of Canada's Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations requires passenger cars, and multi-purpose passenger vehicles, trucks and buses of 4 536 kg GVWR or less, that use a fuel with a boiling point of 0 degrees C or higher, to conform to TSD 301 (Fuel System Integrity). It also applies to school buses above 4 536 kg GVWR.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s301-1.summary: Section 301.1 of Canada's Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations covers vehicles propelled by LPG. They must meet barrier-impact tests under Test Method 301.1 with fuel spillage no more than 142 g, pressure retention in the high-pressure portion of at least 95 per cent, and the container staying attached. Vehicles other than school buses may instead comply with CSA B149.5.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s301-2.summary: Section 301.2 of Canada's Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations covers vehicles propelled by compressed natural gas (CNG). They must meet barrier-impact tests under Test Method 301.2, with the fuel container staying attached and pressure loss limited over 60 minutes. Vehicles other than school buses may instead comply with CSA B109, and CNG cylinders must be marked to CSA B51 Part 2 or ANSI NGV 2.
